source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check ME FW SKU information is normal.
1. Check the information of test item

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ls /sys/class/mei/ 2>&1; echo ---; mei-amt-check -M 2>&1 || echo "ME FW SKU tool not installed"; echo ---; dmesg | grep -iE "sku" | tail -20
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: read the ME SKU (ME FW SKU) via the MEI/SPS channel. The agent collects whatever MEI/SPS registers/dmesg lines are reachable; confirming the value is CORRECT requires knowing the expected value (a user-supplied baseline), so this is PARTIAL: agent returns the raw readout, user judges it against the expected ME FW SKU.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: read-only attempt against Intel MEI/SPS registers using vendor tools (intelmetool / mei-amt-check) that may not be installed on the SUT; install/availability must be confirmed first, and the expected baseline value must be provided by the user.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; requests a baseline but its unverified -M output and generic sku grep do not prove the ME firmware SKU or persistence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; requires exact expected SKU, platform-correlated read-only tooling and one approved reboot comparison.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; treats owner comparison as a capability limit and does not establish source-of-truth identity.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms a returned SKU must be correlated to the SUT and a vendor decoder.

original_test_intent: Read the Intel ME firmware SKU encoded for the identified server platform, compare it with the owner-approved platform/SKU value and verify the same identity persists after an approved reboot.
original_method: Use a documented read-only ME/SPS SKU query with exact platform and firmware identity, retain raw SKU code and vendor decode before reboot, perform one approved controlled reboot, repeat the query and compare expected/pre/post identities.
manual_activity: The owner supplies the expected SKU/decoder, validates the read-only query, approves the reboot and later issues the verdict. All acquisition, reboot, reconnect and comparison steps are electronic and can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact board/SKU, BIOS and ME/SPS generation/firmware identity
Authoritative expected ME firmware SKU code/name and vendor decoder
Approved read-only utility/version/exact syntax and target-selection behavior
Maintenance approval, workload check, reconnect timeout and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not flash, remediate, provision or change SKU/ME state when a mismatch is found.
Do not infer ME SKU from generic kernel text or confuse board/CPU product SKU with ME firmware SKU.
Preserve prior evidence and obtain approval before rebooting.
Stop on ambiguous target/decoder, unexpected SKU, tool side effect or boot/reconnect anomaly; never auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the expected ME SKU and decoder/query; capture board/firmware/MEI identity and raw/decoded pre-reboot SKU.
Perform one approved controlled reboot and monitor downtime/reconnect.
Repeat the identical SKU query, compare expected/pre/post values and collect kernel/BMC/SEL health without firmware changes or a formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Provide the authoritative ME firmware SKU/decoder and approve the diagnostic.
Approve reboot, maintenance and recovery boundaries.
Review identity evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: MEI presence is ancillary, mei-amt-check -M semantics/read-only behavior are unverified and dmesg sku text is not authoritative. The sequence also lacks the post-reboot query.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the platform/vendor-approved read-only ME firmware SKU query and preserve the exact raw code and decode before and after one approved reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ME FW SKU Information normality, persistence after reboot and 5/0-minute fields are preserved without inventing an expected SKU.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the ME SKU field to a vendor code table and collect structured raw/decode output plus exact board and firmware identities using identical pre/post reboot queries.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the ME/SPS generation and board family covered by the supplied SKU decoder.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board revision, BIOS/BMC/ME/SPS, MEI driver, utility, OS and kernel.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use the platform/vendor ME firmware SKU inventory documentation supplied for the target.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact SKU provenance, decoder and the omitted reboot/re-query sequence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; both identity correctness and persistence are retained.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected SKU, decoder and validated read-only query.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Product SKU, firmware image SKU and feature SKU can be distinct; the compared field must be named precisely.

project_override_considerations: A project provides its expected ME firmware SKU and compatible query. This readiness input and engineer verdict do not reduce automation capability; results cannot be generalized across board families.
expected_evidence: Board/SKU, BIOS/BMC/ME/SPS/MEI identities and read-only query-tool manifest
Expected ME firmware SKU code/name and vendor decoder
Raw/decoded pre-reboot SKU, approved reboot/downtime/reconnect transcript and raw/decoded post-reboot SKU
Identity comparison, kernel/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requests correct ME firmware SKU information before and after reboot. Missing expected value and decoder are readiness gaps.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The firmware identity/persistence purpose is clear. Packages and expected SKU can be supplied at project readiness, and the whole technical sequence can be automated.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its missing-baseline warning but rejects generic/unvalidated evidence and PARTIAL classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains platform correlation, safe-tool and reboot safeguards while advancing capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates board/product/firmware SKU identities and preserves mismatch evidence without remediation.

review_improvement: Prevents cross-SKU confusion, adds an auditable code decoder and correctly separates automation capability from owner-provided identity and verdict.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once the expected ME SKU and read-only field query are supplied, every core step is programmatic. Reboot approval and engineer judgment affect readiness and verdict, not capability, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is correct.

no_automatic_retry: One approved pre/post reboot sequence only. Preserve any SKU mismatch, query error or recovery failure and require engineer diagnosis before repeating.
